name: The Dunbar Street Beech
verified_sources: City of Vancouver Heritage Register, category 'LANDSCAPE RESOURCES Trees', heritage_register_id 2543, common name 'Beech', 1711 DUNBAR ST, municipaldesignationm=No, dateoflastupdate 2020-10-14 (opendata.vancouver.ca/explore/dataset/heritage-sites/)

City of Vancouver public-trees open dataset, exact address match '1711 DUNBAR ST', common_name EUROPEAN BEECH, genus FAGUS species SYLVATICA, diameter_cm 133.4, height_m 19.8 (opendata.vancouver.ca/explore/dataset/public-trees/, single record, no other tree listed at this address)
access: Free. Public boulevard tree on the City of Vancouver street right-of-way, reachable and viewable from the public sidewalk at any time.
transport: Residential street in Kitsilano; no transit stop directly at hand, nearest bus service runs along West 4th Avenue a short walk to the south.
verify_notes: Two independent City of Vancouver datasets agree exactly: the Heritage Register lists this address under 'LANDSCAPE RESOURCES Trees' as a Beech with no further detail, and the City's separate public-trees street-tree inventory (a different survey, done for asset management rather than heritage purposes) records a single European Beech at the identical address with a taped trunk diameter of 133.4 cm (about 419 cm / 4.2 m in circumference) and a height of 19.8 m. Only one tree is listed at this address in the public-trees dataset, so there is no ambiguity about which tree the register means. No age or planting date is recorded anywhere and no independent (non-government) write-up was found in the time available, so this is flagged for that reason rather than any factual conflict. A trunk this size is well above a typical urban beech and would repay a look; a girth-based age estimate needs a growth-rate source for Fagus sylvatica in this climate that this pass did not have time to find credibly, so age is left for a reader with a tape measure or a future pass rather than guessed.

name: The West 20th Avenue Spanish Chestnut

location.address: 2003 West 20th Avenue, Vancouver, BC (heritage register gives 2001 W 20th Ave, one house number off; see verify_notes)

verified_sources: City of Vancouver Heritage Register, category 'LANDSCAPE RESOURCES Trees', heritage_register_id 2526, common name 'Spanish Chestnut', 2001 W 20TH AV, municipaldesignationm=No, dateoflastupdate 2020-10-14 (opendata.vancouver.ca/explore/dataset/heritage-sites/)

City of Vancouver public-trees open dataset, address '2003 W 20TH AV' (one house number from the register's '2001'), common_name SPANISH CHESTNUT, genus CASTANEA species SATIVA, diameter_cm 104.1, height_m 19.8 (opendata.vancouver.ca/explore/dataset/public-trees/)
access: Free. Public boulevard tree on the City of Vancouver street right-of-way, reachable and viewable from the public sidewalk at any time.
transport: Residential street in Arbutus Ridge on Vancouver's west side; nearest bus service runs along nearby arterials (Arbutus Street or West King Edward Avenue), a short walk away.
verify_notes: The Heritage Register gives the address as 2001 W 20th Ave; the closest matching tree in the City's separate public-trees street-tree inventory, an exact species match (Spanish Chestnut / Castanea sativa), sits at 2003 W 20th Ave, one house number away, most likely the same tree given odd-numbered addressing along one side of the street and the two-dataset agreement on this being the only chestnut at this end of the block. A second Spanish Chestnut exists further down the same street at 2089 W 20th Ave (124.5 cm diameter) but is too far (roughly a block) to be the same registered tree. Flagged for the address discrepancy, which this pass could not resolve further (e.g. by a street-level photo) in the time available; recorded diameter is 104.1 cm (about 327 cm / 3.3 m circumference), height 19.8 m. No age or planting record found; age left for a reader or a future pass rather than estimated without a growth-rate source.

name: The Blenheim Street Oak
species: Oak (Quercus sp.); heritage register calls it a Pin Oak (Quercus palustris), the City's own street-tree inventory records Red Oak (Quercus rubra) at the same address
verified_sources: City of Vancouver Heritage Register, category 'LANDSCAPE RESOURCES Trees', heritage_register_id 2535, common name 'Pin Oak', 4010 BLENHEIM ST, municipaldesignationm=No, dateoflastupdate 2020-10-14 (opendata.vancouver.ca/explore/dataset/heritage-sites/)

City of Vancouver public-trees open dataset, exact address match '4010 BLENHEIM ST': two Red Oaks (Quercus rubra) recorded, diameter_cm 111.8 and 127.0, height_m 22.9 and 19.8, plus two American Elms and a young hackberry at the same address (opendata.vancouver.ca/explore/dataset/public-trees/)
access: Free. Public boulevard trees on the City of Vancouver street right-of-way, reachable and viewable from the public sidewalk at any time.
transport: Residential street in Dunbar-Southlands on Vancouver's west side; nearest bus service runs along West 41st Avenue or Dunbar Street, several minutes' walk.
verify_notes: Species conflict, not silently resolved: the Heritage Register names this a Pin Oak, but the City's own public-trees street-tree inventory lists no Pin Oak at this address at all, only two large Red Oaks (Quercus rubra), plus two elms and a young hackberry, all at the identical civic address. Given five different trees recorded at one address, it is possible the register's 'Pin Oak' is a data-entry error for one of the two Red Oaks (Pin Oak and Red Oak are both lobed red oaks and are commonly confused), or that the actual Pin Oak stands on the private frontage of the lot and was never captured by the street-tree survey (which covers the public boulevard only). Recorded here is the larger of the two Red Oaks, 127.0 cm diameter (about 399 cm / 4 m circumference) and 19.8 m tall, a genuinely large specimen for either species, on the honest basis that it is very likely the tree the register meant to designate. The page should ask a reader who knows the block to confirm which species is actually standing there. No age or planting record found.
